Belgian road accidents 2017-2024 · focused dashboard

Burden, severity, exposure and regions

289,532 accidents, compared across road-user groups. An accident counts once for every group it involves (road user 1 or 2), so one accident can count for two groups. These are counts, not rates per amount of traffic.

1a

Who is involved

Blue = a named road-user group. Gray = not a specific group (Unknown, Other road user).

Key findings

Fixed text for all years 2017-2024; it does not change with the filters.

  • Passenger cars (70.2% of all accidents) and bicycles (24.8%) are involved most often. Pedestrians follow at 10.3%, vans 8.1%, mopeds 8.0%, motorcycles 6.8%, trucks 4.4%, buses 1.4%.
  • "Unknown" is 10.7%: for about one accident in ten the road user is not recorded.
  • Shares add up to more than 100% because one accident can involve two groups (136,144 accidents involve two different groups).

Read with care: these are raw counts. A group that is common on the road appears often for that reason alone; severity and traffic volume are not part of this graph.

1b

Annual change

Key findings

Fixed text for all years 2017-2024; it does not change with the filters.

  • Almost every group drops in 2020 (bicycles only -5.5%; buses -37.7% and pedestrians -30.4% most) and rebounds in 2021-2022.
  • By 2024 (2017 = 100): bicycles 115, mopeds 105, vans and buses 97, pedestrians 86, motorcycles 83, passenger cars 82, trucks 73.
  • Post vs pre (average per year 2022-2024 against 2017-2019): trucks -17.2%, motorcycles -12.9%, cars -12.2%, pedestrians -10.4%, buses -6.4%, vans +1.5%, mopeds +7.3%, bicycles +14.6%.
  • "Unknown" more than doubles (+113% from 2017 to 2024). Part of the decline of the named groups may be recording shifting into "Unknown"; the data cannot show that.

Read with care: "Covid-19" is my own label for the periods. These are accident counts, not rates, so fewer accidents could also mean less traffic.

2

Severity

Who experiences the most severe outcomes? Fixed results from my analysis scripts, not recalculated here: the years filter on the left does not apply to sections 2 to 4a. The severity class belongs to the WHOLE accident, not to one road user: a car-pedestrian accident counts for both groups.

Period

Share of each group's accidents that are fatal, seriously injured or slightly injured

Dot = share, line = 95% interval, gray line = all accidents. Pre, during and post Covid-19 are my own period names; the data states no cause.

Severity distribution per group

Key findings

Fixed text for all years 2017-2024; it does not change with the controls.

  • Accidents involving trucks and motorcycles are the most severe: fatal plus serious makes up 17.3% (trucks) and 18.9% (motorcycles) of their accidents, against 9.9% for all accidents.
  • The fatal share is 5.1% for trucks (3.6 times the 1.4% of all accidents), 2.8% for motorcycles and 2.0% for pedestrians. It is lowest for mopeds (0.6%), bicycles (0.9%) and passenger cars (1.3%).
  • Bicycle accidents are less often fatal but more often seriously injured (10.0% against 8.4% overall); motorcycles have the highest serious share (16.2%).
  • The fatal share of all accidents falls from 1.54% (2017-2019) to 1.47% (2020-2021) and 1.29% (2022-2024).

Read with care: these are the severity of the accidents a group is part of, not the harm to that group's own members. A truck accident may be fatal mostly for the other party. They are shares given that an accident happened, not the risk of having one. Intervals assume independent accidents, which is slightly optimistic because one accident can count for two groups.

      4a

      Regional severity

      Regional differences in severity: fixed results for all accidents 2017-2024 (the years filter does not apply). The severity class belongs to the whole accident.

      Fatal and serious share per region and province, all accidents. Brussels has no province.

      Province map

      Key findings

      Fixed text for all years 2017-2024; it does not change with the controls.

      • Fatal share: Wallonia 2.26% (1.6 times Belgium), Flanders 1.23%, Brussels 0.42%. Serious-injury share goes the other way: Flanders 9.67%, Wallonia 7.16%, Brussels 4.45%.
      • By province, the fatal share is highest in Luxembourg (3.37%), Namur (2.95%) and Hainaut (2.17%) and lowest in Antwerp (1.04%) and Brussels (0.42%); the serious share is highest in West Flanders (11.5%).

      Read with care: Flanders has more serious but fewer fatal accidents than Wallonia. That could be real or come from how the classes are recorded; I have not tested it.

      About and caveats

      • Data: Belgian road-accident open data 2017-2024 (289,532 accidents), translated to English. One row = one accident (the data has no ID to prove it).
      • Counting: an accident counts for a road-user group if that group is road user 1 or road user 2, once per accident. "Single road user" is not a road user.
      • Unknown (about 10% of accidents, growing over the years) and Other road user are separate lines and hidden by default.
      • Periods: pre (2017-2019), during (2020-2021) and post (2022-2024) "Covid-19" are my own definition; the data states no cause.
      • Counts, not rates: traffic volume is not in the data, so more accidents does not mean more risk per kilometre.
      • Open questions: why empty coordinates jump in Brussels in 2024; the difference between accident classes "with fatalities" and "fatally injured".
      • Not done: urban vs rural. The data has only "built-up area", no official urban/rural classification (decision #55).
      Decisions behind this dashboard: decision log, entries #60-#69, #109-#114, #132-#145 and #163-#167. Code and data: GitHub.
